title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queueing fairness and starvation prevention (timeouts)
author: Ava Thompson
body:
Summary: Tune the continuous-batcher scheduler to improve queueing fairness across priority classes, reduce starvation incidents for low-throughput customers, and introduce configurable per-request timeouts and starvation prevention heuristics. Motivation: Recent production incidents and perf canary runs showed that under mixed workloads (small latency-critical chat vs long background generations) lower-priority requests could be starved for extended periods, impacting SLOs for some customers (see ENG-4982). This PR contains scheduler heuristics and config knobs to balance throughput and fairness while preserving overall GPU utilization.

Changes include: 1) Introduce a per-priority queueing token bucket that ensures minimum dequeue share for each priority class when the system is congested. 2) Add starvation detection: requests that exceed a configurable wait threshold are temporarily elevated in scheduling score for a bounded time window. 3) Implement adaptive dequeue timeouts: long-wait requests receive a shorter per-request CPU-side enqueue timeout to avoid holding slots while waiting for KV cache priming. 4) Refactor the continuous-batcher scheduling loop to separate admission, scoring, and dispatch phases for easier testing and metrics emission. 5) New metrics: batcher.queue_wait_seconds{priority}, batcher.starvation_events_total, batcher.dequeued_with_elevations_total, and batcher.priority_share_estimated. 6) New flags (batcher config): min_share_per_priority, starvation_elevation_ms, dequeue_timeout_ms, enable_priority_hysteresis.

Design notes: - The minimum-share token bucket operates only when active_queue_depth > min_share_threshold to avoid perturbing light-load behavior. - Starvation elevation is bounded (max_elevations_per_request) and decays exponentially to prevent oscillation. - Hysteresis prevents rapid toggling for ephemeral priority changes; we default it off and enable during canary.

Testing: - Unit tests for token bucket and starvation detector. - Integration tests in perf-canary: simulated mixed-workload bench with 80% throughput-background, 20% latency-critical; measured p95 latency improvements and starvation count reductions (see CI bench logs). - Canary rollout: staged to 10% of capacity for 48 hours, then 50%, then 100% after metrics validation.

Rollout and rollback: - Configs are guarded by feature flag and can be tuned at runtime via runtime-config service. - Rollback path is to disable enable_priority_hysteresis and set min_share_per_priority=0 if regressions observed.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests added/updated - [x] Integration bench harness updated - [x] Metrics added - [x] Canary plan documented - [x] Added config defaults and explanation in comments

Impact: Perf canary results show ~18% reduction in p95 latency for low-priority requests under mixed workloads and a ~25% decrease in starvation_events_total. No meaningful throughput regression on large-batch workloads.

Related: ENG-4982, ENG-5010, SUP-1247.

review_comments: Jonas Patel: nits: please add comments explaining the token bucket refill math and why we chose the current refill interval; otherwise LGTM.
Ava Thompson: replied: added comments and referenced a short note in docs/runbooks/continuous-batcher-canary.md explaining the math and trade-offs.
Lina Morales: Concern: elevation could cause priority inversion in certain pathological workloads. Can you add a safety cap per-GPU?
Ava Thompson: replied: added max_elevations_per_request and a global cap evaluated per-worker; updated unit tests to cover the cap.
Marcus Green: Observed a transient CI flake in integration bench around dequeue timeout handling; recommend explicit test for timeout race.
Ava Thompson: replied: added a deterministic timeout test and reworked the dequeue path to avoid holding locks during sleeps.

release_notes: Improve continuous-batcher scheduler fairness and starvation prevention: add per-priority min-share, starvation elevation, adaptive dequeue timeouts, and observability metrics. Canary rollout and runtime flags enabled for fast rollback.
notes: Canary observed ~18% p95 reduction for low-priority under mixed load
Added runtime-config flags so ops can tune without redeploy
No breaking API changes; internal scheduler-only behavior
